highlights.title: Add FreeStyle Libre 3/3+ CGM support
changes: FreeStyle Libre 3/3+ is added to the CGM picker as a beta option.
You can pair Libre 3/3+ sensors directly in Trio without an external app or internet.
The home glucose bobble now shows sensor lifecycle, a warmup countdown, and expiry progress.
LibreLoop sensor alerts appear in Trio and Trio will handle alarms when the CGM has no companion app.
This support is experimental and does not include 1-minute readings.

sources.title: Add LibreCRKit + LibreLoop + LoopAlgorithm submodules; bump CGMBLEKit + OmnipodKit pointers
Register LibreLoopCGMManager and FreeStyle Libre 3/3+ option

highlights.title: Trio 1.0.0 major release
changes: Dosing algorithm moved from JavaScript to native Swift, so calculations are faster and use less battery.
Supports Omnipod 5, FreeStyle Libre 3/3+ (Beta), Eversense E3/365, and Accu-Chek SmartGuide CGMs.
Home screen and chart were rebuilt to let you drag, pinch and scrub up to 72 hours of data.
Alarms, watch and lock-screen forecasts, dosing modes, Quick-Pick treatments, and accessibility were improved.

highlights.title: New Dosing Modes: Open Loop, LGS, Basal Test
changes: A Dosing Mode picker replaces the Closed Loop toggle with Closed Loop, Open Loop, Low Glucose Suspend, and Basal Test.
Open Loop now shows forecasts and updates COB and IOB, and the treatment view works correctly.
Low Glucose Suspend mode can only lower or stop basal insulin and will not give corrective increases.
Basal Testing mode prevents routine adjustments except for low-glucose suspend and pins sensitivity so you can measure.
Switching modes does not change your saved settings and switching back restores your original preferences.

sources.title: nightscout/Trio#1511: Add Trio Dosing Modes: Enhance Open Loop Mode, Add Low-Glucose-Suspend (LGS) and Basal Testing Modes

highlights.title: Fix alarm sounds and Low-Soon alerts
changes: Device alarms now use your selected tone and Play Sound setting when they fire.
Alarm sound files are bundled so system notifications can resolve and play chosen tones.
Delayed critical alarms now start their audio when they actually fire instead of remaining silent.
Low Glucose Soon alerts are evaluated and will fire even when a CGM app handles reading-driven alerts.
On iOS 26+, Trio will use AlarmKit so critical alarms can ring when the app is suspended and pierce Silent/Focus.

sources.title: nightscout/Trio#1375: Fix Alarm  Sounds and Low-Soon Alerts; add AlarmKit for >= iOS 26
Use AlarmKit for critical alarms on iOS 26+

highlights.title: Not-looping alert now escalates over time
changes: Not-looping now escalates in six steps: warnings at 20, 40, 60, 80, and 100 minutes, then Critical at 120 minutes.
All escalation steps are scheduled up front so the Critical alarm still arrives if iOS suspends Trio.
Any successful automated loop clears the entire escalation ladder and restarts the schedule fresh.
Device alarm defaults changed so only Critical alarms play a sound by default; lower tiers are silent banners.

sources.title: Escalate the not-looping alarm instead of firing critical at 20 min

items.title: Show release notes in the app
changes: Home now shows a “New Release” panel when your installed version has unread release notes.
Tapping the panel opens a full-sheet that summarizes what changed and any important safety callouts.
Release Notes are also available from Settings, including a list of previous versions to browse.
Notes are fetched from GitHub with a bundled offline fallback so the notes can load without internet.
Tapping the sheet’s acknowledge button hides the Home panel for that specific version; viewing from Settings does not.

sources.title: nightscout/Trio#1397: Show Release Notes for Installed Trio Version
Show release notes for the installed version

items.title: Glucose Bobble contact image for Contact Trick
changes: Adds a new "Glucose Bobble" contact image layout for the Contact Trick feature.
The Bobble shows a ring, a color-coded glucose number, and a rotating trend arrow.
You can toggle showing minutes-since-reading and showing the glucose delta beneath the number.
You can switch the glucose number between color and monochrome modes.
When Bobble is selected, other contact-image customization options are hidden and stale CGM readings are cleared so the.

sources.title: nightscout/Trio#1473: Adding Glucose Bobble as an optional "Contact Trick" image design.

items.title: Home stats banner uses fixed 180 mg/dL bound
changes: The Home stats banner now uses a fixed 180 mg/dL upper bound.
The banner now matches the Stats screen's Time-in-Range numbers.
Your High Glucose chart threshold no longer changes the banner's upper bound.

sources.title: nightscout/Trio#1421: Use fixed consensus TIR bound in home stats banner

items.title: Suspend/Resume button fixed
changes: The Suspend/Resume button now works correctly in the app.

items.title: Atomic log file appends to prevent lost lines
changes: Log file appends are now written atomically so concurrent writers do not overwrite each other.
Appending to the watch log was updated to use the same atomic write method.
The previous fallback that could replace the whole log file has been removed.

sources.title: nightscout/Trio#1449: Fix non-atomic append in the log file writer
Fix non-atomic append in the log file writer

items.title: Fix forecast lines not drawing in chart
changes: Forecast lines in the main chart now render as connected lines instead of collapsing to points.
This fixes cases where forecast series could disappear on some builds.
The forecast cone and Live Activity visuals are unchanged by this fix.

sources.title: gordolio/Trio#1464: Use unique ids to draw forecast lines
Fix forecast lines rendering nothing by keying ForEach uniquely

items.title: Targets editor fixes wrong mmol/L value
changes: Targets editor now picks the closest glucose value if an exact match is missing when switching units.
Switching from mg/dL to mmol/L no longer shows 4.0 mmol/L for values like 83 mg/dL.
Existing target values are preserved and displayed accurately when changing units.

sources.title: nightscout/Trio#1468: Fix targets editor potentially showing incorrect value of 4.0mmol/L when switching from md/dL to mmol/L

items.title: Centralize override and temp target activation
changes: Overrides and temp targets triggered from the watch, Shortcuts, or remote control now take effect immediately and are (.

sources.title: nightscout/Trio#1482: Centralize override and temp target activation

items.title: Round Nightscout glucose timestamps to ms
changes: Uploaded glucose timestamps are rounded to integer milliseconds before Nightscout upload.
The same instant is used for both date and dateString fields in uploaded records.
The rounding and matching timestamp behavior apply to both sensor and manual glucose entries.

sources.title: nightscout/Trio#1476: Fix fractional Nightscout glucose dates

items.title: Prevent crash when configuring Nightscout CGM
changes: Opening Nightscout configuration from the Home CGM sheet no longer crashes the app.
The Nightscout 'Fetch' and 'Upload' screens now open correctly from that Home sheet.
Settings search highlight behavior is preserved when accessing Nightscout from Home.

sources.title: nightscout/Trio#1483: Fix crash in HomeRootView by injecting the existing SettingsSearchHighlight instance

items.title: Fix bolus and carb label positioning on iOS 27
changes: Bolus and carbohydrate amount labels now appear next to their triangle markers in the chart.
This fixes label misplacement that occurred when building with Xcode 27 / iOS 27.
Marker triangles look the same; only the label anchoring was adjusted.

sources.title: nightscout/Trio#1492: Anchor bolus and carb amount labels to a zero-size companion mark
Anchor bolus and carb amount labels to a zero-size companion mark

items.title: Fix crash when deleting therapy schedule entries
changes: Deleting a time segment in ISF, glucose target, carb ratio, or basal editors no longer crashes the app.
Deleting an entry via swipe, context menu, or VoiceOver now reliably removes it without error.
The time/value picker remains stable if an entry is removed while it is open and will not cause a crash.
The same fix is applied to the four onboarding therapy-setting steps so they behave the same way.

sources.title: nightscout/Trio#1515: Fix index-out-of-range crash when deleting a schedule entry
Fix crash when deleting a therapy schedule entry

items.title: Improve telemetry reliability and privacy
changes: Telemetry uploads are now scheduled to prevent overlapping or duplicate attempts.
Failed telemetry tries are delayed with a one-hour retry backoff.
The app records the prior telemetry failure and includes that context in the next attempt.
If you opt out of full telemetry, the app will still send a minimal anonymous daily check-in with only version, install.
Telemetry requests now include app version and install ID headers and improved app ID parsing to reduce registration 오류.

items.title: Prevent launch crash by delaying telemetry startup
changes: Trio no longer crashes on simulator or debug launches caused by telemetry starting too early.
Telemetry now starts only after the Core Data persistent stores finish loading.
Foreground-transition telemetry checks do nothing until telemetry has been initialized.
Cold-launch telemetry timestamps are recorded about one second later than before.
A remaining race on push-notification cold-launches was left for a follow-up.

sources.title: nightscout/Trio#1519: Fix launch crash: start telemetry after Core Data initialization
Start telemetry after Core Data initialization

items.title: Fix crash opening Target Behaviors
changes: Opening the Target Behaviors settings no longer crashes the app.
The Low Temp Target hint now correctly reflects Basal Testing mode.
Changes to dosing mode are now shown immediately in the Target Behaviors screen.

sources.title: nightscout/Trio#1529: Fix crash when opening Target Behaviors in settings menu

items.title: Fix x-axis label alignment in charts
changes: X-axis time labels on the main chart and all stats charts are correctly aligned again.
The Glucose Distribution (by day) chart's missing x-axis labels are restored and visible.
Percentile and distribution-by-time chart labels are now centered on their marks for clearer alignment.
Removed redundant labels and added glucose units above the Percentile (by day) chart's y-axis.

sources.title: nightscout/Trio#1539: Fix x-axis label alignment in stats and main charts for SDK 27

items.title: Patch: crash fixes and device updates
changes: Several app crashes were fixed, including deleting a therapy time segment, opening Target Behavior, and a Home screen崩溃.
Charts now align correctly and Distribution-by-day labels are shown.

items.title: Round basals to pump's actual supported rates
changes: Basal recommendations are now rounded against the actual paired pump's supported rates.
The pump is handed a bit-exact rate to avoid tiny numeric errors lowering the delivered dose.
An obsolete stored pump model setting was removed so the app no longer falls back to a bundled default.
This prevents unintended small drops in delivered basal rates for affected pumps.

sources.title: nightscout/Trio#1429: Fix Pump Basal Rate Rounding
Round basal rates with the pump's own rate table
Hand the pump a bit-exact basal rate

items.title: Fix DynamicISF crash when autosens min is 1
changes: Fixes a crash when DynamicISF uses the sigmoid option and autosens minimum is set to 1.
The sigmoid calculation now nudges the minimum value so sensitivity ratios adjust with glucose instead of causing an -∞.
As a result, Swift's oref behavior differs from the JavaScript version for this specific edge case.

sources.title: nightscout/Trio#1443: Fixes numerical issue with DynamicISF

items.title: Dosing Mode replaces Closed Loop toggle
changes: The Closed Loop toggle in Settings is replaced by a Dosing Mode picker.
Only Closed and Open modes are offered in Settings right now, with short explanatory hints.
Your existing Closed Loop setting is migrated automatically: true → Closed, false → Open, unknown → Open.
The Manual Temp Basal screen and related controls have been removed.
Onboarding now pre-fills Max IOB to one third of your total daily basal instead of leaving it at zero.

sources.title: nightscout/Trio#1504: [Dosing Modes – Part 1 of 6] Replace the Closed Loop toggle with a Dosing Mode

items.title: Add Low Glucose Suspend and Basal Testing modes
changes: Adds two new dosing modes: Low Glucose Suspend and Basal Testing.
Low Glucose Suspend treats your Max IOB as 0 so Trio will not add corrective insulin.
Basal Testing fixes sensitivity and disables dynamic ISF so you can observe your programmed basals, and only suspends <.
Entering Basal Testing cancels any Trio-set temp basal and Trio will otherwise recommend no temp basals.
These modes are temporary overrides that do not modify your saved preferences, so your settings are restored when you退出.

sources.title: nightscout/Trio#1506: [Dosing Modes – Part 3 of 6] Add Low Glucose Suspend and Basal Testing modes

items.title: Show algorithm's open-loop bolus suggestion
changes: The bolus screen now shows the algorithm's open-loop bolus suggestion.
That suggested amount is reduced by your Recommended Bolus Percentage and capped by Max Bolus.
The suggestion is hidden when the algorithm asks for a basal reduction instead of a bolus.
Open loop still does not deliver the suggested bolus; this only displays the recommendation.

sources.title: nightscout/Trio#1509: [Dosing Modes – Part 6 of 6] Show what the algorithm would give in open loop

items.title: Finalize pump events and record scheduled basal
changes: Pump doses now finalize with actual delivered amounts instead of keeping only the initial command.
Gaps with no pump reports are filled by recorded scheduled-basal rows so the app tracks expected basal delivery.
Scheduled-basal rows are excluded from command inputs and are not uploaded to Nightscout/Health/Tidepool.
Temporary in-flight (mutable) doses update in place until finalized, and uploads send finalized doses only.
TDD totals and the basal chart use recorded delivered values and consume scheduled-basal rows where present.

sources.title: nightscout/Trio#1300: Finalized Pump Events and Infer Scheduled Basal In-Memory

items.title: Fix battery update after switching pumps
changes: Battery percent now updates after switching or onboarding a pump without restarting the app.
The home-screen battery icon shows the new pump's battery immediately after a swap.
The simulator seeds an initial battery row so a battery appears before its first status update.

sources.title: nightscout/Trio#1430: Fix pump battery not updating after pumpmanager swap
Persist pump battery from the delegate callback instead of a status observer

items.title: Unified device picker and pump-based basal steps
changes: Device selection now uses a single grouped picker with manufacturer sections and device icons.
CGM hint lists no longer show unreachable entries like Dexcom Share and FreeStyle Libre Demo.
Onboarding and therapy settings use pump-provided basal increments; Dana now offers 0.01 steps and zero is excluded.
Device icons are resolved from each kit's bundled artwork, with a category glyph fallback for missing assets.

sources.title: nightscout/Trio#1439: Introduce Device Catalog, Refactor Device Pickers and Use Pump-Derived Basal Increments
Add grouped device picker backed by a static catalog
Derive onboarding basal limits from the pump kits

items.title: Eversense CGM update and fixes
changes: Trio can now upload Eversense data to non-US servers.
Trend arrows on E3 sensors display correctly.
Calibration countdown on E3 sensors works correctly.
Eversense sensor insertion dates are uploaded if missing.
Error 255 is hidden and E3 alert history display is fixed.

items.title: Remove Medtronic Enlite CGM
changes: The Medtronic Enlite CGM option is removed from CGM device lists and settings.
Trio will no longer attempt to fetch glucose data from Enlite/Minilink devices.
Enlite-related names and localized strings have been removed from the app.
Enlite is no longer available as a selectable CGM type in setup sheets and dialogs.

items.title: Fix Eversense 365 region handling
changes: Eversense 365 transmitters from Outside US are now supported.
A bug that assigned the wrong region to some Eversense 365 transmitters has been fixed.

items.title: Update device and sensor modules; require iOS 17.6
changes: Device and sensor integration modules were refreshed to newer upstream versions.
OmnipodKit was updated to include an improvement for mid-command disconnects.
Trio's minimum iOS deployment target was raised to iOS 17.6, so a newer iOS is required to run the app.

sources.title: nightscout/Trio#1465: Update submodules to current upstream

items.title: Report dosing mode to Nightscout
changes: Trio now includes the raw dosing mode value in Nightscout device status.
This lets Nightscout followers tell open-loop operation apart from a failed dosing enactment.
The mode is sent as a stable non-localized string so its name does not change with language settings.

sources.title: nightscout/Trio#1508: [Dosing Modes – Part 5 of 6] Report the dosing mode to Nightscout

items.title: Stop dropping display-only glucose readings
changes: Trio no longer drops glucose readings that are marked as display-only.
Display-only readings are now stored so they can be used by the loop.
Sensor-reported faulty readings are still withheld and not stored.
Libre 3/3+ sensors that previously had their display-only readings discarded will now have those readings accepted.

sources.title: nightscout/Trio#1512: Fix for Libre 3/3 Plus: Stop dropping display-only glucose readings

items.title: Submodule updates: OmnipodKit PKA and fixes
changes: Pod keep‑alive behavior for Omnipod BLE pods is improved.
Unwanted silent beeps on O5 Omnipod devices are reduced.
Connection reliability is improved for some Omnipod and iPhone setups.
Standing CGM alerts are retracted when a CGM device is removed.
Minor algorithm and pump handling fixes were applied to insulin calculations and dosing records.

sources.title: nightscout/Trio#1549: Update submodules to current upstream 18-09-2026

items.title: Basal rate pill shows current pump delivery
changes: The basal rate pill now shows what the pump is actually delivering (suspended, temp, or scheduled).
The app reports the scheduled basal rate even when the pump has no history yet.
Manual temp basals are flagged with a hand icon and an accessibility label indicating a manual basal.
The chart's basal profile line is drawn immediately when the chart appears.

sources.title: nightscout/Trio#1556: Fix stale basal rate on home chart

items.title: Show real pump failure instead of blaming authentication
changes: The app shows the pump's real reason when a Quick-Pick bolus fails, instead of always blaming Face ID/Touch ID.
If carbs were logged but the bolus failed, the alert will include the pump's failure message when available.
If biometric authentication actually failed, the app still shows the authentication error message.

sources.title: Show the pump's real failure reason for a failed Quick-Pick bolus instead of always blaming authentication

items.title: Tamer alarms and no more duplicate sounds
changes: Alarm tones were equalized so different alerts no longer vary wildly in loudness.
If the system alarm channel is already sounding an alert, the notification is posted silently to avoid the same sound播放.
Alarms no longer force the device volume to maximum and only raise it to a moderate floor when needed.
Alarm availability is checked early so alarms don't accidentally play twice before the app is ready.

items.title: Updated looping indicator spinner
changes: The loop indicator now uses a spinning capsule animation instead of the old progress view.
The "looping" label is shown verbatim only while the spinner is actively animating and is not localized.
The spinner will continue briefly after looping stops to avoid flicker and enforces a short minimum spin time.
Stroke thickness and sizing animations for the spinner were refined for a smoother appearance.

sources.title: nightscout/Trio#1251: upgrade looping animation and remove looping text
upgrade looping animation and remove localization for looping text

items.title: Improve localized settings and header layout
changes: Verbose settings hints now wrap and expand vertically so descriptive text is no longer cut off and is left-aligned.
Many settings and configuration screens now show their hint text with consistent left alignment and spacing.
Home screen header layout was adjusted to prevent overlaps and better position the pump/CGM and glucose panels.
Watch complication code was restricted so the corner complication is only used on watchOS, improving device-specificity.

sources.title: nightscout/Trio#1408: Fix localized settings hint layout

items.title: Stable contact image backgrounds
changes: You can pick a background for contact images (Transparent or Black) in the contact image editor.
Choosing Black prevents contact images from randomly switching between white and black backgrounds.
Transparent background preserves image transparency while Black fills the image area with solid black.
Your chosen background is saved with each contact image and restored when shown.

sources.title: nightscout/Trio#1427: fix for contact backgrounds having unstable background colours

items.title: Show quick-pick bolus with one decimal
changes: Quick-pick bolus suggestions now display with a single decimal place.
Suggested amounts are floored to one decimal (rounded down) instead of rounded to nearest.
This prevents the suggestion pill from showing two fractional digits.

sources.title: nightscout/Trio#1431: Floor quick-pick bolus suggestions to one decimal place

items.title: Accessibility and VoiceOver improvements
changes: VoiceOver now speaks status, charts, and icon-only buttons in plain words.
Controls that previously required gestures can now be activated with VoiceOver actions.
Glucose bobble and charts now read a single, combined summary with value, trend, delta, and age.
Text scaling is bounded to prevent very large fonts from breaking layouts.
Glass panels and small UI chrome switch to opaque, higher-contrast fills when Reduce Transparency or Increase Contrast.

items.title: Restore looping spinner and pull-to-refresh UI
changes: Loop indicator now shows a standard spinner and the text "looping" when active.
The previous animated capsule spinner was removed and replaced by a simpler spinner layout.
Pull-to-refresh now displays a spinner with the label "Forcing loop…" while forcing a loop.
Forcing a loop remains visible for at least one second and the dashboard shifts down to make room.

sources.title: nightscout/Trio#1436: Revert "upgrade looping animation and remove looping text"

items.title: Glass-styled action sheets replace confirmations
changes: Confirmation dialogs across the app now open as a bottom glass-style action sheet instead of the system popover.
Sheets use a frosted “Liquid Glass” panel appearance with a bold, detached Cancel button.
When Reduce Transparency is enabled the sheets fall back to opaque panels and a stronger dim behind them.
Action labels are localized correctly and dynamic names are shown verbatim where needed.

sources.title: nightscout/Trio#1393: Introduce Custom Liquid Glass-Styled Action Sheet as Confirmation Dialog Replacement

items.title: Localization updates including Simplified Chinese
changes: Many user-facing strings were updated with new or improved translations across languages.
Simplified Chinese (zh-Hans) translations were added for numerous app texts.
Several localized messages had wording or punctuation corrected in various languages.
These updates may change the text you see in non-English locales, including prompts, alerts, and settings.

items.title: Watch: Log Carbs fallback when bolus is zero
changes: If the recommended bolus is zero, the watch shows a "No Bolus, Log Carbs" button so you can log carbs without a bolus.
Turning the insulin dial above zero restores the "Enact Bolus" button and opens the bolus confirmation flow.
Tapping the "No Bolus, Log Carbs" button logs the carbs from the watch and shows an acknowledgment screen.
The watch shows a "Calculating Bolus..." progress state while waiting for the phone and clears it on reply, error, or a.
The insulin amount is snapped to the configured increment so tiny dial residues do not count as a non-zero bolus.

sources.title: nightscout/Trio#1450: Add watch "Log Carbs" fallback when recommended bolus is zero

items.title: Chart selection moved to meal row
changes: Selection readout appears in the meal row instead of a floating card, so it no longer covers chart data.
Selection time is shown on the chart x-axis under the indicator instead of inside the readout.
Scrubbing no longer re-lays the chart and selection markers stay aligned during pinches and drags.
The readout briefly persists across small data gaps instead of flickering back to live IOB/COB while scrubbing.
The readout uses a glass-styled compact row and shows glucose, smoothed value, and IOB/COB inline.

items.title: Localization updates and translation fixes
changes: Updated many user-visible strings across multiple languages so app text is more complete and accurate.
Added and completed Italian translations for numerous app labels and messages.
Corrected and clarified Simplified and Traditional Chinese text for many labels and prompts.
Fixed wording, spacing, and punctuation in several languages and added new locale entries to improve localized UI.

items.title: Remote meals stop showing the text note
changes: Remote carb entries no longer include the text "Remote meal command" as a note.
Remote carb entries are now marked with a satellite symbol (📡) instead of the text note.

sources.title: nightscout/Trio#1469: Enter remote meals without a note

items.title: Glucose plotted above carbs and boluses
changes: Glucose lines are now drawn on the top chart layer so carbs and boluses no longer hide them.
Some alarm- and intent-related text entries were added or updated in the app localizations.

sources.title: nightscout/Trio#1470: Plot glucose on the top chart layer so carbs and boluses no longer hide it

items.title: Refreshed Pump and CGM settings screens
changes: Pump and CGM settings screens use a cleaner list layout with improved spacing and background styling.
Connected pumps and CGMs appear as larger centered buttons showing the device image and name.
Add Pump and Add CGM actions are more prominent and include a help button with device hints.
The Smooth Glucose help text was rewritten with clearer bullet points explaining smoothing behavior.

sources.title: nightscout/Trio#1471: fix: styling pump & cgm screens

items.title: Localization and alarm permission message updates
changes: The app now includes a new alarm permission message explaining why alarms are used.
Many in‑app texts and translations were updated across multiple languages.
Several Chinese translations and other wording were corrected for clarity.
Accessibility and time/number strings were refined for localized formats.

items.title: Chart gestures added to Chart Legend
changes: The Chart Legend now includes a new "Chart Gestures" section.
It describes drag, pinch, double-tap, and press-and-hold chart actions.
Each gesture entry shows a short explanation and an icon.
The chart legend was reorganized into labeled sections for clearer reading.

sources.title: nightscout/Trio#1493: feat/gesture-legend add explanation of gestures

items.title: Loop pill shows open-loop state and device health
changes: The loop pill no longer claims to be looping when Trio is in open loop.
In open loop the ring reports device health: green while CGM and pump report, red on device issues.
The time caption is shown only in closed loop and is hidden in open loop to avoid implying an action.
The loop icon is now an open ring with horizontal gaps and a centre symbol for constrained modes, and it scales with a�.
Pull-to-refresh can no longer force a loop when Trio is in open loop.

sources.title: nightscout/Trio#1505: [Dosing Modes – Part 2 of 6] Stop the loop pill claiming to loop in open loop

items.title: Show active dosing mode in loop status
changes: The loop status sheet now shows the active dosing mode.
Each mode shows a short note about its action (open: no pump command; LGS: may only lower basal; Basal Testing: holds).
Help text and the glossary now note that Dynamic ISF is disabled during Basal Testing.
Status badge text color is fixed so it remains readable in dark mode.

sources.title: nightscout/Trio#1507: [Dosing Modes – Part 4 of 6] Name the dosing mode in the loop status sheet

items.title: Hide home statistics panel option
changes: You can hide the home statistics panel so it only shows a "View Statistics" shortcut.
When showing averages, the banner now spells out "Avg. Glucose" instead of using the ⌀ symbol.
Settings text was updated to describe the Hide Statistics option and the available panel choices.
Tapping the statistics panel still opens the full statistics view.

sources.title: nightscout/Trio#1518: Add option to hide home stats panel metrics

items.title: Localization updates and new translated strings
changes: Updated many in-app text translations in multiple languages, especially Portuguese (pt-PT).
Added new localized labels for treatments and UI items such as carbs, fat, protein, insulin, GMI, and mode status.
Adjusted wording in several translations, including a French phrasing change for the Add button.
Added explanatory Color Mode text and other accessibility-focused strings.

items.title: Fix blank Loop Mode help sheet and clarify LGS hint
changes: Loop Mode help sheet no longer opens blank the first time you tap it.
Help sheet content is now presented reliably on first open.
Low Glucose Suspend help text now warns that insulin delivery may resume if IOB goes negative.

sources.title: nightscout/Trio#1523: Fixing Loop Mode help sheet
Clarify LGS hint: basal may resume if IOB goes negative

items.title: Rename Previous Versions to Release Notes
changes: The Settings item labeled "Previous Versions" is now labeled "Release Notes".
The release notes screen title now shows "Release Notes" instead of "Previous Versions".

sources.title: nightscout/Trio#1541: Rename "Previous Releases" button to "Release Notes"

items.title: Fix grid toggle spacing in settings
changes: The two grid toggles in User Interface settings no longer touch at small text sizes.
The Y-axis grid toggle now has added top spacing in the Home view settings screen.

sources.title: nightscout/Trio#1575: Fix home view toggle placement

items.title: Internal dependency-injection cleanup
changes: There are no user-facing feature or UI changes.
Internal service setup was simplified to remove unused injections and duplicate resolves.
Several background services are now created and shared by a central container instead of self-managing singletons.
Automated tests were added so missing or mis-scoped service registrations fail CI instead of causing launch-time issues.

sources.title: Clean up DI: dead injections, singletons into container

items.title: Use GitHub teams for code owner assignments
changes: Pull request reviewer assignments now use GitHub team groups instead of a single global list.
Code ownership is organized by component so different teams are auto-assigned for different parts of the repo.

sources.title: nightscout/Trio#1513: Update CODEOWNERS to use github groups

items.title: Trio v1.0.0 major release
changes: Trio has a new major release labeled v1.0.0.
The release changes were merged back into the development branch.

sources.title: nightscout/Trio#1527: MAJOR RELEASE Trio v1.0.0 – Sync back to Dev

items.title: Add @nightscout/ prefix to CODEOWNERS groups
changes: The repository's CODEOWNERS file now includes the @nightscout/ prefix on all team names.
Team ownership entries for core algorithm, pump drivers, CGMs, CI, and translations were updated.
This only changes who is automatically requested for code reviews and does not affect the app's behavior.

sources.title: nightscout/Trio#1531: Add '@nightscout/' prefix to CODEOWNERS groups

items.title: Sync v1.0.1 patch release to dev
changes: The codebase was updated to include the Trio v1.0.1 patch release.
Release branch changes were merged back into the development branch.

sources.title: gordolio/Trio#1564: PATCH RELEASE Trio v1.0.1 – Sync back to Dev

includedPullRequests.title: Finalized Pump Events and Infer Scheduled Basal In-Memory
includedPullRequests.body:
## Summary

Adopts LoopKit's dose lifecycle for pump event storage and records scheduled basal delivery instead of inferring it per consumer. Scheduled basal rates (SBRs) are kept mostly for Trio-internal convenience.

  - **Upsert by dose `syncIdentifier`**: mutable (in-flight) events update in place; finalized reports freeze rows with actual `deliveredUnits` and run times. Previously we kept the commanded first report and dropped the finalized one. Also fixes same-timestamp bolus+TBR shadowing in dedup.
  - **Adopt `replacePendingEvents`**: unasserted mutable rows are revoked (LoopKit `DoseStore` semantics); this should avoid any orphaned doses. Uploads (NS/Health/Tidepool) now send finalized rows only, once.
  - **Scheduled basal recorded** (`isScheduledBasal`): a reconciler fills reporting gaps (open loop, connectivity loss, TBR expiry) from the basal schedule each loop tick; pump-reported data always wins and overlapping synthetic rows self-heal.
  - **Consumers**: TDD sums recorded rows and `deliveredUnits` (inference removed); chart plots SBR segments at reduced opacity; oref input and `currentTemp` intentionally exclude them (commands only); NS is not uploaded SBR rows.

**Migration:** additive optional attributes, lightweight (verified on a populated store with ~1k records of existing pump data). Legacy rows count as finalized, non-scheduled. Verified on pump+CGM sim: mutable and subsequent finalized on same row, 5.7h gap backfilled at schedule rates, TDD/chart/loop work / plot nominally with SBR rows present.

Follow-ups / Left-over TODOs: 
* Health/Tidepool pseudo-event consolidation
* Potentially address open-suspend at 24h look-back boundary (fetch 24 hrs of data, excluding suspend event)

includedPullRequests.body:
## Summary

This PR tidies up dependency injection and adds tests to guard the container wiring.

- Dependency injection cleaned up by dropping unused `FetchGlucoseManager` injections and the orphaned `Router` resolve in `DeviceDataManager`, and dedupes eager resolves in `loadServices`. `TrioRemoteControl`, `TelemetryClient`, and `TelemetryAttestor` are now registered container-scoped instead of self-resolving static singletons, which removes the lazy-inject lock ceremony they required.
- Adds container resolution specific tests to check resolve of every eagerly loaded service and assert that the converted singletons stay identical across resolves. A missing or mis-scoped registration now fails in CI rather than at launch.

Blocked by #1300.

includedPullRequests.title: Fix Alarm  Sounds and Low-Soon Alerts; add AlarmKit for >= iOS 26
includedPullRequests.body:
Alarm sounds never reached the user. Four independent causes, one per commit.

Fixes #1371
Fixes #1428

### Causes

1. Device Alarms config (tone, Play Sound, Override Silence & Focus, day/night window) stopped being applied to catalog-known alerts in `00bdcb84b`; only the interruption level survived the switch to catalog routing. Plugins issue alerts with `sound: nil`, so device alarms had no tone at all.
2. Tones shipped as an Xcode folder reference, so they built to `Trio.app/Sounds/`. `UNNotificationSound(named:)` resolves only against the bundle root and `Library/Sounds`, so iOS silently substituted the default sound. The picker preview and `CriticalAlertAudioPlayer` worked because they were the only paths passing `subdirectory: "Sounds"`.
3. The critical-audio fallback, which is what pierces the silent switch and Focus without the Critical Alerts entitlement, rejected anything not `.immediate`. The not-looping watchdog is the only `.delayed` alert Trio creates, so the one alarm that fires unattended never got audio.
4. `evaluateForecast` bailed on the same CGM-ownership guard as the reading path, so Low Glucose Soon was never evaluated on Dexcom, xDrip4iOS or Libre, where "Use CGM App Alerts" defaults on.

### Commits

| Commit | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `86061e0` | Register the 18 `.caf` files individually so they flatten to the bundle root; drop the now-wrong `subdirectory:` from both lookups. Vendor sounds move to a flat `Library/Sounds/<manager>-<file>`. |
| `1420ca6` | Start playback from the modal scheduler's timer, whose `.insert` decision already means live, not stale, not snoozed. `.immediate` still plays at issue time. |
| `22dbce0` | Drop the CGM-ownership guard from `evaluateForecast`. A CGM app cannot compute Trio's oref forecast, so it can never cover this alarm. `evaluateCarbsRequired` already omits it, and the settings screen only moves reading-driven types into "Handled by CGM App". |
| `cdc46d2` | AlarmKit for critical alarms on iOS 26+, ported from Loop's `CriticalAlertAlarmScheduler`. Needs no entitlement and still fires when iOS has suspended Trio. Plays the user's selected tone. Stop acknowledges the alert rather than only silencing it. |

Earlier commit `690f24f0` (opt-in Critical Alerts entitlement) was dropped from this branch.

### Coverage

| Case | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Critical, immediate, app running | default iOS sound | selected tone, pierces silent + Focus |
| Critical, delayed (not-looping) | silent | selected tone at fire time |
| Critical, app suspended, iOS 26+ | not possible | AlarmKit, selected tone |
| Critical, app suspended, iOS 17-25 | not possible | still not possible without the entitlement |

### Testing

Full suite green, 565 tests / 82 suites. New tests assert every `AlarmSoundCatalog` filename resolves via `Bundle.main.url(forResource:withExtension:)`, the call shape iOS uses, so a folder reference cannot silently regress this again.

Not covered by tests, needs a device: tone actually playing, piercing Silent and Focus, AlarmKit ringing on a suspended app, Stop acknowledging the alert. The AlarmKit custom tone in particular is unverified here.

includedPullRequests.title: Show Release Notes for Installed Trio Version
includedPullRequests.body: ## Summary Surfaces Trio's release notes in two places: - **Home** — a "New Release" entry in the multi-use panel, opening a sheet the user acknowledges to dismiss it - **Settings → Release Notes** — the current release, plus a **Previous Versions** screen for earlier ones ## Where the notes come from Three sources, in order of preference: 1. A live fetch of the GitHub releases API, since notes are sometimes edited after publishing 2. The last successful fetch, cached 3. A copy bundled at build time by `scripts/capture-release-notes.sh` The bundle covers **every stable release back to the last major or minor bump**, building `0.8.4` embeds `0.8.0` through `0.8.4`, so the list still works on a phone that has never been online. That script can never fail a build. A missing release, an unreachable GitHub, an unparseable version or an empty environment all simply leave the fallback out; every path exits 0, and a stale bundle from a previous version is removed rather than left behind. Drafts, prereleases, anything newer than the running build, and anything before `0.8.0` are all excluded. Sorting is by version. ## What the sheet renders The release's opening prose, its GitHub alert callouts, and the bullets under **"What's Changed At A Glance"**. The full notes, including the pull request lists, stay on GitHub behind a link. Two things worth knowing, both found by testing the parser against real releases rather than assuming a format: - **The "At A Glance" heading is not universal.** Five of the six most recent releases have it; the `0.8.3` hotfix used "What happened" / "What's fixed" instead. Relying on that heading alone would have produced an empty sheet on exactly the kind of urgent hotfix people most need to read, so the parser falls back to the release's opening prose. - **Releases carry `[!IMPORTANT]` callouts with safety-relevant content** — *"If you are using Medtrum Nano please update at your earliest convenience"*, *"your active Pod will be automatically transitioned"*. A bullets-only sheet would have hidden these behind a browser link, so they are parsed and shown. ## Acknowledgement Stored per version, so installing a newer release surfaces the panel again with nothing needing to reset it. Only the sheet's button acknowledges — swiping it away, or browsing notes from Settings, leaves the panel in place. The panel ranks below every warning state and above the stats. `MultiUsePanelState.resolve` gained a parameter, so its existing tests were updated and three added for the new ordering; all 10 pass. ### Screenshots | ☾ Release Panel | ☀ Release Panel | Settings Row | Release Notes | |--------|--------|--------|--------| | | | | |

includedPullRequests.title: Fix Pump Basal Rate Rounding
includedPullRequests.body:
## Summary

As reported in #1424, `TempBasalFunctions.roundBasal` erroneously considered every pump to one hardcoded set of supported basal rates, 0.025 below 1 U/hr, 0.05 to 10, 0.1 above, which is actually a Medtronic x23/x54’s rate... Further, `profile.model` was read from `settings/model.json`, a file that was never ever written to disk. As a consequence, every algorithm run fell back to the bundled `"722"`

  ### Changes

  1. **Drop the unused pump model setting.** `Profile.model`, both `ProfileGenerator parameters, the `createProfiles` load, `Settings.model`, and the bundled `settings/model.json`.
  2. **Round with the actual pump's own supported rates.** `roundBasal` floors against a new non-persisted
     `Profile.supportedBasalRates`, injected per algorithm run from the paired driver in `OpenAPS.determineBasal`. This mirrors LoopKit's `PumpManager.roundToSupportedBasalRate`, so the rate the algorithm commits to is the rate the pump delivers / can actually deliver.
  3. **Round the closed-loop dose before delivery as an additional safety net.** `performBasal` and `performBolus` handed the determination to the driver unrounded, unlike their `enactTempBasal` / `enactBolus` twins in APSManager.

Adjusted unit tests accordingly.

Fixes #1424.

### Update

@mountrcg found that point 3 was wrong: `Foundation`'s `Decimal` → `Double` conversion can land just below the value (0.07 becomes 0.06999999999999999), and since every pump table floors, re-rounding at delivery dropped a full increment on 41 of Dana's 301 rates. Two follow-up commits:

- **Hand the pump a bit-exact rate.** `performBasal` / `performBolus` now convert via the decimal string, which is bit-identical to the driver's own table entry, and no longer re-floor — the algorithm already floored against the same table. The `roundToSupportedBasalRate` comparison stays as a log-only canary. The algorithm side was never affected: it stays in `Decimal` end to end.
- **Fix a test type-check timeout on Xcode 26.2**, which CI pins. Both jobs are green.

`BasalRoundingDriverParityTests` now walks every entry of all five kit tables through the real delivery path, with a regression pin on 0.07 / 0.14 / 1.99 against `Double(truncating:)`.

includedPullRequests.title: Fix pump battery not updating after pumpmanager swap
includedPullRequests.body:
BaseAPSManager registers itself as a PumpManagerStatusObserver at init. This means if the pump manager is replaced without an app relaunch (i.e. switching pumps) the observer stays bound to the previous instance.

The delegate is re-attached in DeviceDataManager's didSet, so reservoir/dose/status data kept flowing, but the observer-driven storeBatteryStatus never ran for the new pump -- no OpenAPS_Battery rows were written and the home battery icon stayed hidden until relaunch.

Fix by having DeviceDataManager emitspumpManagerDidChange from the pumpManager didSet (where the delegate is already re-attached), covering every assignment path. APSManager re-registers its status observer on that signal.

includedPullRequests.title: Introduce Accessibility Improvements
includedPullRequests.body:
## Summary

This PR introduces broad accessibility improvements  across the entire app, focused on VoiceOver support, Dynamic Type limits, and Reduce Transparency / Increase Contrast fallbacks. The goal throughout is to make status, controls, and charts that currently rely on color, icons, or gestures readable and operable for assistive-technology users.

The main areas covered:

- **Status readouts spoken in words** — loop pill, pump reservoir/battery/pod, IOB/COB, alarms, eventual glucose, and Nightscout/Tidepool connection state now announce their meaning instead of color and icon names. The glucose bobble reads value, range, trend, delta, age, and sensor warmup/expiry as one element.
- **Controls made operable via VoiceOver** — slide-to-confirm quick bolus (previously drag-only, which blocked delivery), stop-adjustment / stop-temp-target / stop-override cancels, tappable header panels, and picker rows across settings, onboarding, statistics, alarms, and therapy editors.
- **Grouped, labeled content** — recommendation-math cards, bolus-progress readouts, stat summaries, and settings value rows read as single coherent phrases; icon-only buttons (help, hint, add/remove, dismiss, time nudge, etc.) get spoken labels; decorative icons and row dots are hidden.
- **Charts named** — glucose, forecast, basal, carb-ratio, ISF, target, calibration, and the twelve statistics charts get VoiceOver labels.
- **Dynamic Type bounded app-wide** — capped at accessibility1 globally (tighter at xxLarge on the dense Statistics screen) so large text scales without breaking layouts.
- **Glass chrome fallbacks** — glass panels and small material affordances fall back to an opaque, higher-contrast fill under Reduce Transparency or Increase Contrast.

## Additional notes

This PR depends on #1332 and should not be merged until that lands.
Addresses #1351. 

## Reviewing

This is a rather large PR (**16 commits, 85 files**), but each commit is self-contained and scoped to a specific area or screen. **Please review commit-by-commit** rather than viewing the full diff. That keeps each change in context and makes the scope far easier to follow.

includedPullRequests.title: Fixes numerical issue with DynamicISF
includedPullRequests.body:
If DynamicISF is using sigmoid and has a autosensMin value == 1 then
there are numerical issues with log10 returning -Inf, causing a crash
loop (https://github.com/nightscout/Trio/issues/1441).

The fix is to add a fudge factor to avoid this case, similar to what
JS oref had for a divide by zero when autosensMax == 1.

Important: This change will cause Swift's oref to behave differently
from JS. JS will simply default to a ratio of 1 for all cases when
autosesnsMin == 1, with this (very hacky) fix the Swift implementation
will product ratios that adjust as glucose changes (see unit tests).

Moving forward we should strongly consider replacing sigmoid with a
straight line -- they just aren't that different in practice and a
straight line is much easier to implement and understand, which is a
big deal given two hacks to work around numerical issues and some
random 0.0555 in the algorithm. But that will be for a future PR.

includedPullRequests.title: Add watch "Log Carbs" fallback when recommended bolus is zero
includedPullRequests.body:
In the watch "Meal & Bolus" flow, the bolus screen's only action was "Enact Bolus", disabled whenever the amount was 0 U. A 0 U recommendation is a normal outcome (low glucose, stale loop, or IOB already covering the meal), so the user hit a dead end: back out to the root, choose "Meal", and re-enter the carbs.

Now, when carbs were carried in from the combo flow and the insulin dial sits at zero, the button becomes "Log Carbs" and logs the carbs directly (matching the standalone "Meal" path). Dialing insulin above zero flips it back to "Enact Bolus" and the existing crown-confirm path is unchanged. The zero check is taken against the increment-snapped amount so floating-point residue from dialing the crown up and back down does not read as a non-zero bolus.

To keep a fast tap from logging carbs before the phone's recommendation arrives, requestBolusRecommendation() now drives the existing (previously unused) "Calculating Bolus..." progress state, cleared on reply, on send error, or after a 3s timeout.

Demo video on simulator: https://www.youtube.com/shorts/o-QPaloI03A

includedPullRequests.title: Use unique ids to draw forecast lines
includedPullRequests.body:
### Problem

`ForecastView.drawForecastsLines()` keyed its `ForEach` on `\.id`:

```swift
ForEach(preprocessedData, id: \.id) { tuple in
```

That id isn't unique per row. `fetchForecastHierarchy` mints one `UUID()` per
*forecast*, and `ForecastSetup` stamps it onto every value in that forecast — so
~240 rows share ~5 identities. Duplicate ids in a `ForEach` are undefined
behaviour; SwiftUI may collapse them, leaving each series a single point and a
`LineMark` nothing to connect.

The cone is unaffected (`ForEach(0 ..< n, id: \.self)`), as is the Live Activity,
which uses the same unique-index pattern.

### Fix

```swift
ForEach(preprocessedData, id: \.forecastValue.objectID) { tuple in
```

Every row is a distinct `ForecastValue` managed object, so its `objectID` is
unique by construction and stable across fetches — no allocation, no positional
identity. Series grouping comes from `foregroundStyle(by:)`, not `ForEach`
identity, so lines neither merge nor split.

### Why it needs a fix

It seems we've just been lucky until now, but building with Xcode 27 causes the forecast lines to not display at all in the main chart because of this.

includedPullRequests.title: Centralize override and temp target activation
includedPullRequests.body:
This rewrite was done because overrides activated from the watch were not sent to Nightscout until they were cancelled. The change has successfully been tested in real-world use for several days with no issues.

Shortcuts, remote control and the watch route activation and cancellation through AdjustmentManager, which performs the whole sequence in one Core Data transaction: end every enabled adjustment and record each as a run entry, enable the requested one, then apply the side effects in a fixed order. Commands are serialized, so two arriving at once cannot interleave. The Adjustments view keeps its own write path in this PR.

The run entry carries the elapsed duration to Nightscout and draws the finished band on the home chart. uploadOverrideRuns deletes the entry at the run's own created_at and re-posts it there, so the cleanup holds for a preset row whose date moves on every activation, and the run upload window keys on endDate so an adjustment that ran for more than a day still retracts its placeholder. deleteNightscoutOverride filters on event type.

APSManager.determineBasalSync() is the single entry point for a determination outside the loop. It waits for a loop in flight to finish, collapses concurrent calls into one, never delays a loop start, and keeps throwing so the treatment views still see algorithm errors. The manager and the Adjustments view models go through it.

A custom, non-preset adjustment is stored disabled and activated by object ID, so storeTempTarget returns the inserted row's NSManagedObjectID.

The watch acknowledges a command from the returned outcome, and its failure acknowledgment applies only to messages carrying none of the recognized payloads. A remote cancel with nothing running is the state the command asked for.

Fix fractional Nightscout glucose dates
includedPullRequests.body:
Fixes https://github.com/nightscout/Trio/issues/1478

## Summary

- round stored glucose timestamps to integer milliseconds before Nightscout upload
- use the same timestamp for `date` and `dateString`
- cover both sensor and manual glucose records

## Problem

`getGlucoseNotYetUploadedToNightscout()` converted `Date.timeIntervalSince1970` to `Decimal` before multiplying by 1000. This preserved sub-millisecond precision and produced values such as `1788785143203.7996` in Nightscout.

Nightscout can return that value as `lastModified.collections.entries`, while clients expect an integer millisecond timestamp.

## Testing and verification
- Added a regression test with a fractional timestamp. It verifies that sensor and manual Nightscout records use the rounded integer millisecond value and keep the same `dateString` instant.
- I also verified this by running my Trio build and inspecting the entries uploaded to my own nightscout instance

includedPullRequests.title: Fix crash in HomeRootView by injecting the existing SettingsSearchHighlight instance
includedPullRequests.body:
`NightscoutUploadView` and `NightscoutFetchView` require a `SettingsSearchHighlight` environment object that is missing when Nightscout configuration is opened from the Home-screen CGM sheet.

Cause of the crash is https://github.com/nightscout/Trio/commit/5cb78b6af0bae7751167527160d7f9232a9559b2 which added `.settingsHighlightScroll()` to these two views.

- Both destinations apply `.settingsHighlightScroll()`
- That modifier unconditionally reads  `@Environment(SettingsSearchHighlight.self)`
- The object is injected only into the Settings tab’s `NavigationStack`
- The Home-screen CGM sheet is outside that subtree, so navigating to Upload or Fetch causes SwiftUI’s fatal “no observable object of type `SettingsSearchHighlight` found” failure
- Settings to Services to Nightscout works because that route inherits the required environment object

So we can inject the existing settings-highlight environment into the Home CGM sheet so the Nightscout child routes inherit it, without changing the working `Settings` navigation path.

PR fixes the crash in `HomeRootView.swift` by injecting the existing `SettingsSearchHighlight` instance into the Home-screen CGM configuration sheet. Nightscout’s Upload and Fetch views now inherit their required environment dependency.

Fixes #1480 

**Test steps:**
1. Enable nightscout as a CGM (you may need to delete your existing CGM and set up nightscout as the CGM)
2. Click on your CGM and configure nightscout, then go to 'Fetch' or 'Upload' and verify the subscreens open without crashing

includedPullRequests.title: Fix for Libre 3/3 Plus: Stop dropping display-only glucose readings
includedPullRequests.body:
`isDisplayOnly` means the reading was shifted for visual consistency after calibration (LoopKit), not that it is unsafe to dose on: Loop keeps these samples and excludes them only from momentum and counteraction. The gate was LibreLoop-scoped, so Trio already dosed on Dexcom's display-only samples.

It never held either way: LibreLoop's backfill paths forward the same sensor minute with isDisplayOnly false, so a dropped reading re-entered unflagged. On Libre 3 Plus the actionability bit is stuck clear, so every reading was discarded and those users could not loop at all.

**Readings the sensor reports as faulty are still withheld by the driver.**

Fixes #1495 and similar reports.

includedPullRequests.title: Fix index-out-of-range crash when deleting a schedule entry
includedPullRequests.body:
## Summary

Deleting a time segment in the ISF, glucose target, carb ratio or basal editor could kill the app with `Fatal error: Index out of range`. 

The fix takes index bindings out of the therapy settings item row entirely:

  - `ForEach(items)` iterates values, so `item.id` in an action is a captured `UUID` rather than a binding read
  - `deleteItem(with:)` resolves the index by id at call time — used by the swipe action, the context menu and the VoiceOver delete action (which previously also read `item.id` through the binding)
  - the picker row gets an id-keyed binding whose setter no-ops if the entry is gone
  - `validateTherapySettingItems()` keeps ids stable; selection falls back to time-matching only when the selected entry
  actually disappeared

This fix touches the shared editor for all therapy settings, so it covers ISF, glucose target, carb ratio and basal editors as well as the four onboarding therapy-setting steps.

Fixes #1497

includedPullRequests.body:
I noticed that server-side telemetry logs showed 50x more requests to /api/auth/ios/challenge (the pre-step for telemetry emit to get an updated token) than /checkin (the step which actually emits the telemetry).

This seems to be because of:
```

2026-09-13T21:08:49-0400 [Telemetry] TelemetryClient.swift - send(reason:) - 401 - DEV: register failed: unable to read application-identifier entitlement — will retry next cycle
```

This causes only the /api/auth/ios/challenge request to be made, and not /checkin, which is what actually stores the telemetry.

In this PR:

- Adds safer telemetry scheduling so cold launch, foreground, timer, and CGM background triggers cannot overlap or double-send. Add trigger context like cold_launch, foreground, timer, background_activity, build_change, or manual.
- Adds one-hour retry backoff after failed telemetry attempts so failures do not retry continuously.
- Records and reports the previous telemetry failure category on the next request.
- Adds App Attest identity/context headers to telemetry server requests:
    - X-Trio-Version
    - X-Trio-InstallId
- Improves App ID/provisioning profile parsing for forks, custom bundle IDs, TestFlight/sideload builds, and malformed profiles.
- Adds an opted-out daily anonymous heartbeat using an empty GET /anonymous, carrying only version/install/reason/failure context. This new light-telemetry allows us to track total users without any additional identifying information captured, and does NOT flow into the regular telemetry pipeline. It just lets us roughly estimate the total user count which has telemetry disabled via server side request count.
- Adds focused tests for send gating, retry backoff, URL/query construction, identity headers, App ID parsing, and anonymous request shape.

I noticed that server-side telemetry logs showed 50x more requests to /api/auth/ios/challenge (the pre-step for telemetry emit to get an updated token) than /checkin (the step which actually emits the telemetry).

This seems to be because of:
```

2026-09-13T21:08:49-0400 [Telemetry] TelemetryClient.swift - send(reason:) - 401 - DEV: register failed: unable to read application-identifier entitlement — will retry next cycle
```

This causes only the /api/auth/ios/challenge request to be made, and not /checkin, which is what actually stores the telemetry.

In this PR:

- Adds safer telemetry scheduling so cold launch, foreground, timer, and CGM background triggers cannot overlap or double-send. Add trigger context like cold_launch, foreground, timer, background_activity, build_change, or manual.
- Adds one-hour retry backoff after failed telemetry attempts so failures do not retry continuously.
- Records and reports the previous telemetry failure category on the next request.
- Adds App Attest identity/context headers to telemetry server requests:
    - X-Trio-Version
    - X-Trio-InstallId
- Improves App ID/provisioning profile parsing for forks, custom bundle IDs, TestFlight/sideload builds, and malformed profiles.
- Adds an opted-out daily anonymous heartbeat using an empty GET /anonymous, carrying only version/install/reason/failure context. This new light-telemetry allows us to track total users without any additional identifying information captured, and does NOT flow into the regular telemetry pipeline. It just lets us roughly estimate the total user count which has telemetry disabled via server side request count.
- Adds focused tests for send gating, retry backoff, URL/query construction, identity headers, App ID parsing, and anonymous request shape.

includedPullRequests.body:
## Summary 
This PR moves the six reviewed parts (#1504, #1505, #1506, #1507, #1508 and #1509) into dev. Each was reviewed and merged individually; this is the integration PR.

It replaces the **Closed Loop toggle** with a Dosing Mode picker: Closed Loop, Open Loop, Low Glucose Suspend, Basal Testing. Each mode carries an AutomationLevel, `off` / `hypoSuspendOnly` / `reductionsOnly` / `full` (i.e. closed-loop).

  - Open Loop is now a "real mode": Trio surfaces forecasts, COB and IOB update properly, treatment view is fully functional. Closes #643.
  - Low Glucose Suspend: Trio may only lower or stop basal, never correct a high. See also: https://androidaps.readthedocs.io/en/3.1/Configuration/Config-Builder.html#low-glucose-suspend-lgs
  - Basal Testing: Trio does no adjustment at all unless glucose actually goes low, with sensitivity adaptation pinned so the user can actually measure their basal profile.

The constrained modes work by clamping the algorithm's inputs, not the user's settings. Stored preferences always remain unchanged, so switching back restores everything and manual bolusing keeps honoring real Max IOB. Verified on real device(s) during testing.

 Closes #644.

includedPullRequests.title: Fix launch crash: start telemetry after Core Data initialization
includedPullRequests.body:
## Problem

Debug/simulator launches of current dev crash within seconds:

```
NSInternalInconsistencyException: This NSPersistentStoreCoordinator has no persistent stores (unknown). It cannot perform a save operation.
```

Crashing queues are `NSManagedObjectContext: storeGlucose` and `storeBatteryStatus`.

## Cause

Since #1367, `TelemetryClient.shared` resolves through the DI container with eager `injectServices`. `AppDelegate.didFinishLaunchingWithOptions` calls it at launch, which resolves `APSManager` + `FetchGlucoseManager` and thereby constructs `BaseDeviceDataManager` — the whole APS/device graph — **before** `CoreDataStack.initializeStack()` has finished loading the persistent stores.

The CGM and pump **simulators** deliver status/readings immediately on construction, so their first Core Data save races the store load and aborts the app. Real hardware usually wins the race (BLE reconnect latency), which is why reports cluster on simulator-configured dev setups; a Debug/TSAN build widens the window further. The launch-order log signature: a healthy launch logs `Successfully loaded persistent store` *before* `PumpManagerState` is persisted; a crashing one persists `PumpManagerState` immediately and never reaches the store-load line.

## Fix

`AppDelegate` no longer resolves services at launch (only the Crashlytics gate remains, which touches plists only). Telemetry starts at the end of `TrioApp.loadServices()` — i.e. strictly after Core Data initialization — with the identical cadence sequence as before (install ID, cold-launch recording, SHA-change ping, recurring timer, overdue check). The foreground-transition hook receives its `TelemetryClient` reference from `loadServices()` and no-ops before that.

This deliberately does **not** reintroduce the old `injectIfNeeded` deferral; eager injection stays, only the call site moves behind the initialization barrier.

## Notes

- Cold-launch timestamps are now recorded ~1 s later (post store load) — immaterial to the 7-day sliding window.
- A latent same-class race remains on the APNS path (`TrioRemoteControl.shared` in `didReceiveRemoteNotification` when a push cold-launches the app). It predates #1367 and is left for a follow-up.

includedPullRequests.body:
For detailed release notes, see: https://github.com/nightscout/Trio/releases/tag/v1.0

## What's Changed At A Glance

- **Trio thinks in your iPhone's "own language" now** – the dosing algorithm was rewritten from JavaScript into native Swift; identical decisions, twice as fast, easier on your battery
- **Omnipod 5** – full support, including the guided first-pod setup (requires one-time internet connection)
- **FreeStyle Libre 3 and 3+ (Beta)** – paired directly in Trio, with no companion app and no internet connection needed to loop
- **Eversense E3 and 365** – the implanted sensor family, with optional upload to Eversense DMS
- **Accu-Chek SmartGuide** – Roche's 14-day sensor, now a first-class Trio CGM
- **A rebuilt Home screen** – drag, pinch and scrub through up to 72 hours of data in Trio's chart, with one smart panel that surfaces whatever needs your attention
- **A Modernized Look** – Liquid Glass has made its way to Trio, making it look like a proper iOS 26+ app
- **Alarms you can actually hear** – four separate bugs were silencing them; on iOS 26 and later, critical alarms now sound even when iOS has put Trio to sleep
- **Dosing Modes** – the Closed Loop switch becomes a four-way choice: Closed Loop, Open Loop, Low Glucose Suspend and Basal Testing
- **Quick-Pick Treatments** – Trio learns the amounts you actually use and puts them one tap away
- **Forecasts on your wrist and lock screen** – the glucose prediction now appears on the Apple Watch app and in the Live Activity
- **Garmin complications** – put glucose, IOB and COB on any Connect IQ watch face
- **Built for everyone** – massively improved accessibility pass across VoiceOver, Dynamic Type and contrast
- **Release notes inside the app** – read what changed without leaving Trio
- **Steadier under the hood** – a large reliability pass on data storage, background work and pump event handling
- **Anonymous diagnostics are on by default** – no health data is ever sent, and opting out is one tap in Settings

includedPullRequests.body:
For detailed release notes, see: https://github.com/nightscout/Trio/releases/tag/v1.0

## What's Changed At A Glance

- **Trio thinks in your iPhone's "own language" now** – the dosing algorithm was rewritten from JavaScript into native Swift; identical decisions, twice as fast, easier on your battery
- **Omnipod 5** – full support, including the guided first-pod setup (requires one-time internet connection)
- **FreeStyle Libre 3 and 3+ (Beta)** – paired directly in Trio, with no companion app and no internet connection needed to loop
- **Eversense E3 and 365** – the implanted sensor family, with optional upload to Eversense DMS
- **Accu-Chek SmartGuide** – Roche's 14-day sensor, now a first-class Trio CGM
- **A rebuilt Home screen** – drag, pinch and scrub through up to 72 hours of data in Trio's chart, with one smart panel that surfaces whatever needs your attention
- **A Modernized Look** – Liquid Glass has made its way to Trio, making it look like a proper iOS 26+ app
- **Alarms you can actually hear** – four separate bugs were silencing them; on iOS 26 and later, critical alarms now sound even when iOS has put Trio to sleep
- **Dosing Modes** – the Closed Loop switch becomes a four-way choice: Closed Loop, Open Loop, Low Glucose Suspend and Basal Testing
- **Quick-Pick Treatments** – Trio learns the amounts you actually use and puts them one tap away
- **Forecasts on your wrist and lock screen** – the glucose prediction now appears on the Apple Watch app and in the Live Activity
- **Garmin complications** – put glucose, IOB and COB on any Connect IQ watch face
- **Built for everyone** – massively improved accessibility pass across VoiceOver, Dynamic Type and contrast
- **Release notes inside the app** – read what changed without leaving Trio
- **Steadier under the hood** – a large reliability pass on data storage, background work and pump event handling
- **Anonymous diagnostics are on by default** – no health data is ever sent, and opting out is one tap in Settings

Fix x-axis label alignment in stats and main charts for SDK 27
includedPullRequests.body:
Fixes #1525 

## Summary

Building Trio with Xcode 27 to iOS 27 shifts x-axis labels out of alignment across the
statistics charts and the main chart, and hides them entirely on the glucose
Distribution (by day) chart.

Three Swift Charts behaviours changed in the iOS 27 SDK. Each is gated on the
**linked SDK**, not the OS: the same source built with Xcode 26 renders
correctly on an iOS 27 device, so this only started affecting users once Trio
was built with Xcode 27.

| Swift Charts API | Behaviour under SDK 27 |
|---|---|
| `AxisValueLabel(centered: true)` | Centres across the span to the next *labelled* mark instead of one stride unit |
| `AxisValueLabel(anchor:)` | Silently ignored unless `preset: .aligned` is also set |
| `.chartYAxisLabel` | Consumes the x-axis label row when combined with `.chartScrollableAxes` |

## Changes

**SDK 27 fixes**

- **Stats charts** — every chart strides finely and labels sparsely (stride by
  day, label weekly), so the `centered:` change pushed labels right by half the
  *label* spacing: ~3.5 days in month view, ~half a month in 3M, 3 hours in day
  view. Five near-duplicate axis blocks are replaced with one
  `StatChartUtils.dateAxisMarks(for:)` that emits an `AxisValueLabel` on every
  stride value — empty where no label is wanted — so "next labelled mark" once
  again equals "next stride value". That is correct under both the old and the
  new semantics, and a no-op on iOS 26. The mark closing the domain is left
  unlabelled so `preset: .aligned` stops pinning its centred label on top of the
  preceding one (the `TueWe` overlap in week view, the stray clipped `0` in day
  view).
- **Main chart** — already passed `anchor: .top`; adding `preset: .aligned`
  makes it take effect again. Verified the glucose, basal and COB/IOB panes stay
  column-aligned: gridline positions are identical across all three panes with
  and without the preset.
- **Distribution (by day)** — this is the one chart that is both scrollable and
  used `.chartYAxisLabel`, so it is the only one whose x-axis labels disappeared.
  Removing the label fixes it; a y-axis label cannot be reinstated on that chart
  while it is scrollable.

**Deliberate changes (not regressions)**

- **Centre on-mark labels** — Percentile/Distribution by time and Looping
  Performance had left-aligned labels sitting ~5pt right of their mark on *every*
  SDK. They are now centred via `preset: .aligned` + `anchor: .top`.
- **Label cleanup** — dropped the redundant "Percentage" labels and the
  "Glucose Distribution" heading, and added the glucose units above the y-axis of
  Percentile (by day), which had none.

Bar charts keep `centered: true` throughout: their labels measure 0px from bar
centre, which is the right target for a bar. Only point/area charts centre on the
mark.

## Testing

Each configuration was measured against rule marks placed at the exact target
position, on the iOS 26.5 and iOS 27.0 simulators, built against both SDK 26.5
and SDK 27.0:

| | SDK 26.5 build | SDK 27 build, before | SDK 27 build, after |
|---|---|---|---|
| `centered:` span | 0px | +115px | 0px |
| `anchor: .top` | 0px | +32px | 0px |
| main chart | 0px | +32 to +36px | 0 to −1px |

The old and new label-selection logic were also compared exhaustively — 90 days
of axis marks × all four intervals × both original code paths — with zero
unintended differences; the only changes are the intended trailing-mark trims.

includedPullRequests.title: Adjust Not-Looping Alerts Escalation
includedPullRequests.body:
## Summary

Changes the not-looping alert from a single 20 min critical alarm into a six-step escalation scheme:

* Time-Sensitive at 20, 40, 60, 80, and 100 min
* Critical at 120 min
* All six are armed up front as OS notifications, so escalation still works if iOS ever suspends Trio
* Any successful loop retracts the full ladder and starts fresh

Each warning gets its own alert ID (`w1`…`w5`) because pending notifications with the same identifier replace each other rather than stack.

Also updates device alarm defaults:

* Critical defaults to sound on, using `high_chimes.caf`
* Time-Sensitive and Normal default to silent
* Decode fallback now follows the per-tier default
* Glucose alarm sound defaults are unchanged

Tests were updated for the new ladder and sound defaults, and the unused `AlertMuter.allowedDurations` was removed.

### Note

Existing persisted device alarm settings are left untouched, so current users keep their existing `playsSound` / `soundFilename` values. Moving them to the new defaults would need an explicit migration.
